instruction: Install and configure Varnish with multiple backends
output:
<think>
Goal: The goal is to configure cat correctly for this use case.
The configuration involves multiple parameters — we'll apply them together for consistency.

Plan: I'll use `cat` as the primary tool — cat command execution and management. `systemctl` will be used for manage systemd services and units. `host` will be used for host command execution and management.

Precautions: SERVICE CONSIDERATION: Restart services during maintenance windows. Check unit dependencies beforehand with `systemctl list-dependencies`. Verify the result with a follow-up `cat — check the output matches expectations.
</think>
cat > /etc/varnish/default.vcl << 'EOF'
vcl 4.1;
backend web1 { .host = "192.168.1.10"; .port = "80"; }
backend web2 { .host = "192.168.1.11"; .port = "80"; }
sub vcl_recv {
  set req.backend_hint = web1;
  if (req.restarts > 0) { set req.backend_hint = web2; }
}
sub vcl_backend_response {
  set beresp.grace = 1h;
}
EOF && systemctl reload varnish
